content.title: About
content.content: Ground chicken with additives is minced chicken meat to which salt, spices, stabilizers and other food additives may be added. The product is sold raw and intended for further cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ground chicken is a staple in many cuisines, from patties to stuffed vegetables.
Additives may include antioxidants that extend the product’s shelf life.
Raw ground chicken has a shorter shelf life than processed sausages.
Proper grinding yields a uniform texture ideal for shaping burgers and kebabs.
Chicken meat is considered more diet‑friendly than beef due to its lower fat content.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Ground chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with beef mince, chicken contains less saturated fat, making it a healthier choice.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Ground chicken offers iron, zinc and phosphorus important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Chicken proteins are quickly digested, beneficial for people with higher nutritional needs.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Raw ground chicken may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter, so keep it at 0‑4 °C and cook to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.

items.title: Allergy to additives
items.content: Some additives (e.g., monosodium glutamate) can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt raises sodium levels, which should be considered by people with hypertension.

items.title: Not suitable for infants
items.content: Raw ground chicken can be hard to digest for babies and poses a food‑borne illness risk.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use the mince for patties, meatballs, vegetable fillings, dumplings and sauces. Mix thoroughly, season as desired, and cook until the internal temperature reaches at least 75 °C.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the mince in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for 1‑2 days. For longer storage freeze at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge, not at room temperature.
